'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**[[Catatumbo campaign]]
***[[2025 Catatumbo clashes]]
****Eighty-four [[National Liberation Army (Colombia)|National Liberation Army]] (ELN) combatants surrender to [[Colombia]]n [[Military Forces of Colombia|authorities]] as offensive operations resume in the [[Catatumbo region]]. Colombian authorities also rescue 20 [[child soldiers]] from the ELN's 33rd Front. [https://www.elcolombiano.com/colombia/primeros-resultados-operaciones-militares-en-el-catatumbo-GE26447188 (''El Colombiano'')]
**A [[National Police of Colombia|police officer]] is shot dead by an ELN sniper in [[Río Iró]], [[Chocó Department]], Colombia. [https://www.eltiempo.com/colombia/otras-ciudades/choco-muere-patrullero-de-la-policia-que-resulto-herido-durante-ataque-armado-del-eln-en-rio-iro-3420870 (''El Tiempo'')]
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[January 2025 Gaza war ceasefire|2025 Gaza war ceasefire]], [[Gaza war hostage crisis]]
***[[Israeli Defense Forces|Israeli forces]] open fire on a crowd of [[forced displacement|displaced]] [[Palestinians]] waiting at the [[Netzarim Corridor]], killing two people and wounding seven others, including a child. [[Government of Israel|Israeli authorities]] allege that the shooting was due to the delayed release of Israeli hostage [[January 2025 Gaza war ceasefire|Arbel Yahud]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/2-killed-7-injured-by-israeli-army-fire-in-gaza-in-violation-of-ceasefire/3462678 (Anadolu Ajansi)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/program/newsfeed/2025/1/25/israeli-forces-fire-on-crowds-near-gazas-netzarim-corridor (Al Jazeera)]
***[[Hamas]] frees four [[Israelis|Israeli]] hostages, including [[Kidnapping of Naama Levy|Naama Levy]], in exchange for 200 [[Palestinian prisoners in Israel|Palestinian prisoners]], including 121 people serving [[life sentence]]s after being convicted of carrying out deadly attacks against Israelis, as part of the ceasefire deal. [https://apnews.com/article/israel-palestinians-hamas-war-news-ceasefire-hostages-01-25-2025-150674e17bd8b22f2c2c3aa4991cf061 (AP)]
**[[Israel]] accuses Hamas of violating the deal by failing to release female civilians, including Arbel Yehud, before [[Women in the Israel Defense Forces|female soldiers]]. As a result, Israel blocks Palestinians from returning to [[North Gaza Governorate|North Gaza]] through the Netzarim Corridor. [https://apnews.com/article/israel-palestinians-hamas-war-news-ceasefire-hostages-01-26-2025-d0f9d113ceec2dababe462967ee8d398 (AP)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c9qjy4lzqn3o (BBC News)]
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[M23 offensive (2022–present)|M23 offensive]]
***Thirteen [[peacekeeping|peacekeeper]]s, including nine from [[South Africa]], three from [[Malawi]] and one from [[Uruguay]], are killed as fighting intensifies in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] between [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|government forces]] and [[March 23 Movement|M23]] rebels, the latter backed by the [[Rwanda Defence Force|Rwandan military]]. [https://www.lemonde.fr/en/le-monde-africa/article/2025/01/25/13-peacekeepers-killed-as-fighting-rages-in-eastern-drc_6737423_124.html (''Le Monde'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Siege of El Fasher]]
***At least 70 people are killed in a [[drone warfare|drone attack]] on the Saudi Hospital, one of the last functioning hospitals in [[El Fasher]], [[Sudan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/sudan-war-hospital-attack-fasher-53f41de57ca442ed5dd3a8a1312f4052 (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Eighteen people are killed and ten more injured in a [[gasoline]] [[tank truck]] explosion along an [[Controlled-access highway|expressway]] in [[Enugu State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://apnews.com/article/nigeria-tanker-explosion-gasoline-f2b546036ef8a0b4b1360333aed972f3 (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda tensions (2022–present)]]
**The [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] severs its [[diplomatic relations]] with [[Rwanda]] as Rwandan-backed rebels advance on the city of [[Goma]], the capital of the DRC's [[North Kivu]] province. [https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2025/jan/25/rwandan-army-ready-to-invade-drc-and-help-rebels-seize-city (''The Guardian'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Islam and blasphemy]], [[Capital punishment in Pakistan]]
**A [[Pakistan]]i court sentences four people [[death sentence|to death]] for [[blasphemy]], after they allegedly posted sacrilegious material on social media about [[Islam]]ic [[Islamic religious leaders|religious figures]] and the [[Quran]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2025/01/25/pakistan-court-sentences-4-people-to-death-for-blasphemy (Al Arabiya)]
*[[2025 Drents Museum heist]]
**A heist at the [[Drents Museum]] in [[Assen]], [[Netherlands]], results in the loss of valuable [[Dacians|Dacian]] gold and silver artifacts, including the [[Helmet of Coțofenești]]. [https://www.dutchnews.nl/2025/01/interpol-drafted-in-to-help-in-dacia-gold-heist-investigation/ (Dutch News)] [https://www.romania-insider.com/romanian-dacian-treasure-robbery-dutch-museum-january-2025 (''Romania Insider'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 Greek presidential election]]
**The [[Hellenic Parliament]] fails to elect the new [[President of Greece]]. A second round is called between the candidates [[Konstantinos Tasoulas]] and [[Louka Katseli]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/greek-lawmakers-fail-elect-new-president-first-round-voting-2025-01-25/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2025 Australian Open]]
**In [[tennis]], [[Madison Keys]] wins her first [[Grand Slam (tennis)|major]] title after defeating the two-time defending champion [[Aryna Sabalenka]], 6–3, 2–6, 7–5, to win the [[2025 Australian Open – Women's singles|women's singles]] title at the [[Australian Open]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2025/01/25/sport/australian-open-womens-final-sabalenka-keys-spt-intl/index.html (CNN)]
**[[Henry Patten]] and [[Harri Heliövaara]] defeat [[Simone Bolelli]] and [[Andrea Vavassori]] 6–7 (16–18), 7–6 (7–5), 6–3, in the [[2025 Australian Open – Men's doubles|men's doubles final]] to win their first Australian Open title and their second joint Grand Slam title. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/articles/c9vmdkzd9k2o (BBC News)] [https://ausopen.com/articles/news/mens-doubles-heliovaarapatten-win-dramatic-decider (AO)]
**[[Kateřina Siniaková]] and [[Taylor Townsend]] defeats [[Hsieh Su-wei]] and [[Jeļena Ostapenko]] 6–2, 6–7 (4–7), 6–3, to win the [[2025 Australian Open – Women's doubles|women's doubles final]] title.
